title: Torsion-free groups inject into their rationalization
statement: Let $G$ be an abelian group such that $m g=0$ for an integer $m>0$ implies $g=0$. The canonical homomorphism from $G$ to its rationalization $G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ [def-trf-rational-rank], $g\mapsto g\otimes 1$, is injective.

source.place: §2.1, pp. 7–8, rationalization of the ordered value group; the elementary torsion-free tensor fact is made explicit here.

proof.text: Put $S=\mathbf Z\setminus\{0\}$, which contains $1$ and is closed under multiplication. Use the fraction construction of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. The map $S^{-1}\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q$, $a/s\mapsto a/s$, is a ring isomorphism: every rational has a nonzero integer denominator, and the localization relation $u(ta-sb)=0$ for some $u\ne0$ is equivalent to $ta=sb$, exactly rational-fraction equality. The addition and multiplication formulas agree. In particular $a/1$ maps to the integer $a$ in $\mathbf Q$.

source.place: Tags 00CN (definition-multiplicative-subset) and 07JZ (definition-localization-module), preceding fraction construction; elementary identification of the fraction field of Z with Q.

proof.text:
The universal property and generation clause of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] give inverse $\mathbf Z$-linear maps $\mu:\mathbf Z\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G	o G$, $a\otimes g\mapsto ag$, and $
u:G	o\mathbf Z\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G$, $g\mapsto1\otimes g$. Indeed $\mu
u(g)=g$ and $
u\mu(a\otimes g)=1\otimes ag=a\otimes g$ by bilinearity. By [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], their localizations have formulas $(a\otimes g)/s\mapsto ag/s$ and $g/s\mapsto(1\otimes g)/s$; their composites are identities on every fraction because $\mu
u$ and $
u\mu$ are identities.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property and bilinearity; Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module), induced maps on fractions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] with $R=A=\mathbf Z$, $T=S$, $M=\mathbf Z$ and $N=G$. It gives an isomorphism $S^{-1}(\mathbf Z\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G)\to S^{-1}\mathbf Z\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G$, $(a\otimes g)/s\mapsto(a/s)\otimes g$. Combine its inverse with Step 2 and the ring identification of Step 1. Interchanging the tensor factors gives inverse maps $\mathbf Q\otimes_{\mathbf Z}G\rightleftarrows G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$: they send $q\otimes g$ to $g\otimes q$ and back, are well-defined by the bilinear universal property of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and their composites fix every generating pure tensor. Thus we obtain an additive isomorphism $\theta:S^{-1}G\to G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ satisfying $\theta(g/s)=g\otimes(1/s)$, and in particular $\theta(g/1)=g\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 00DK (lemma-tensor-localization), with the existing general base-ring localization-tensor leaf; Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product) for the explicitly written symmetry maps.

proof.text: Let $g,h\in G$ satisfy $g\otimes1=h\otimes1$. By Step 3, $(g-h)/1=0$ in $S^{-1}G$. The kernel criterion in [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] gives a nonzero integer $s$ with $s(g-h)=0$. If $s>0$, the hypothesis gives $g-h=0$ directly. If $s<0$, then $(-s)(g-h)=-s(g-h)=0$ and $-s>0$, so the same hypothesis gives $g-h=0$. Consequently $g=h$. Bilinearity shows that $g\mapsto g\otimes1$ is the canonical additive homomorphism, so this proves its injectivity.

source.place: Tag 07JZ (definition-localization-module), fraction relation and kernel criterion; Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), bilinearity; elementary application of the stated torsion-free hypothesis.
